findings.violation: This field's type, name, or id identifies the street-address input purpose, but it carries no autocomplete token, so the purpose is not programmatically determinable.
findings.fix: Set the field's autocomplete attribute to street-address, or the matching standard token for this input purpose.

findings.violation: This field's type, name, or id identifies the tel input purpose, but it carries no autocomplete token, so the purpose is not programmatically determinable.
findings.fix: Set the field's autocomplete attribute to tel, or the matching standard token for this input purpose.

findings.location: "label.required-label", the two required-field labels, lines 27 and 30
findings.evidence: <label class="required-label" for="address">Service address</label>, styled by .required-label { color: #cc0000; }; no asterisk, no required text, and no aria-required attribute appears on either field
findings.violation: Which fields are required is carried by label color alone, so a reader who cannot distinguish the red labels from the black ones has no way to tell the two required fields from the two optional ones before submitting.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal to each required field: mark the label text itself (an asterisk with a legend, or the word required), and set required or aria-required on the input.

findings.location: "main > p:nth-of-type(2)", the instructional paragraph above the form, line 24
findings.evidence: Fields shown in red are required. Everything else is optional.
findings.violation: The instruction identifies the required fields only by their color, naming no label, no field, and no other identifier a reader who cannot perceive the color could use instead.
findings.fix: Name the required fields in the instruction, or point at the same non-color marker added for WCAG-1.4.1, for example fields marked with an asterisk are required.

findings.location: "span.error-text", the error message following the account-number field, line 38

findings.fix: Replace the error text with one that names the field and the rule it failed, for example account number must be the 8 digits printed above your billing address.

note: The other three goldens document scripted-lane-only output; this one shows what the judged lane looks like on the same contract, now alongside two scripted WCAG-1.3.5 findings rather than one. The callback-number field (id=phone, type=tel, no autocomplete) was already the single in-scope field WCAG-1.3.5 caught before cue-word matching was added; the service-address field (id=address, type=text) now also lands in scope, since address is a FORMS cue word for the street-address purpose even though it is not the literal token itself. Two in-scope fields failing escalates BOTH WCAG-1.3.5 findings to severity 3 under references/WCAG.md's recurrence anchor, a known consequence of cue-word matching rather than a defect golden-05.html was built to plant. The form signals required fields with red label color and nothing else otherwise, which is WCAG-1.4.1's severity-3 anchor case because a color-blind reader cannot separate required from optional until submission; the instruction above the form then compounds it by pointing at that same color as its only identifier, which is WCAG-1.3.3 at severity 2 since every field still carries a readable text label. The Details heading fails WCAG-2.4.6 at severity 2, and it is reported at medium confidence rather than high because a generic heading is a judgment about what the section actually contains, which is exactly the calibration references/severity-anchors.md asks the judged lane to make. The account field is marked invalid with an error reading only the word Error, which WCAG-3.3.1 puts at severity 2 for a single field. Findings are ranked by severity, then by criterion ID, per the four-pass protocol's rank-and-bound step, and the three severity-3 findings (two scripted WCAG-1.3.5, one judged WCAG-1.4.1) fail the gate against the default zero threshold.
